mission.cluster: the Hns computer-use goal/success/capability/destructive-mode/limit/plan execution contract and its typed failure codes

adaptation: CommonJS -> ESM JavaScript, one target module per donor file boundary (`constants.cjs` -> `contracts.mjs`, `errors.cjs` -> `errors.mjs`, `action.cjs` -> `action.mjs`, `criteria.cjs` -> `criteria.mjs`, `contract.cjs` -> `contract.mjs`), plus `index.mjs`, which is a barrel over those five boundaries and adds no behaviour. The donor's own `app/computer-use/index.cjs` is not ported (it wires controllers, drivers, the executor and the evidence log, which belong to this building's other modules and to the executor that consumes them). Donor names, field order, closed vocabularies, thresholds, precedence, comments and message strings are carried over as they were; only the language and the two adaptations below changed.

LOAD-PURITY ADAPTATION (mandatory). The donor `constants.cjs` was load-impure: it imported `node:fs` and `node:path`, computed `const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..')` at module load, and read `<ROOT>/config/app.json` inside `readComputerUseConfig(root = ROOT)`. That init-time read was the *default argument* of `resolveComputerUseOptions(overrides, configBlock = readComputerUseConfig())`, so every caller silently picked up the shipped `computerUse` block. In the port, `resolveComputerUseOptions(overrides = {}, configBlock = {})` takes the already resolved config block as a PARAMETER; the module reads no file, no `__dirname`, no `process.cwd`, and does not import `node:fs` or `node:path`. The parameter's `{}` default is exactly the donor's catch branch (`catch { return {} }`, the 'missing or damaged config file' path), so the donor's two-argument call shape still resolves identically when no block is supplied. The donor's `ROOT` and `readComputerUseConfig` exports are consequently NOT ported: the parameter replaces the file read, and `ROOT` only existed to locate that file. `contract.mjs` forwards the block through a third `createContract(input, options, configBlock = {})` parameter, because the donor's `createContract` called `resolveComputerUseOptions(options)` with one argument; the two-argument donor call now behaves like the donor's empty-config branch.

TARGET DEPENDENCY SEAM. The donor `action.cjs` and `contract.cjs` imported `normalizeTarget` / `describeTarget` from `app/computer-use/target.cjs`. The City manifest assigns `target.cjs` to the sibling module `target-guard` (`mb-008-target-guard-lab`), whose boundary covers target normalization, the fixed resolution ladder, revalidation thresholds and matching. That module is NOT part of this port. Because action normalization and `safety.forbidden_targets` cannot work without those two pure helpers, and this module may not add files or depend on a sibling that is landing concurrently, the two helpers (`normalizeTarget`, `describeTarget`) and their private support (`TARGET_KINDS`, `KIND_BY_NAME`, `build`, `targetKinds`, `normalizeRect`, `normalizePoint`, `normalizeWindowRef`, `compact`, `looksLikeSelector`, `invalidTarget`) are reproduced in `action.mjs`, verbatim in behaviour and message strings, and exported from there for `contract.mjs`. `resolveTarget`, `revalidate`, the matching rungs and the revalidation thresholds are NOT ported here and remain `target-guard`'s. `target-guard/target.mjs` landed concurrently while this module was being built; a 3 000-vector comparison shows the two implementations agree on every accepted input and on every `describeTarget` label, so the duplication changes no result. Re-importing from the sibling would couple this module to another module's internals and is deliberately not done under a MIGRATION_ONLY port.

Purity of the ported modules: no filesystem, network, clock, `Math.random`, `process.env`, timer or `require` access anywhere. No time or id is read or generated by this contract surface (the donor's own contract path generates neither), so nothing had to be injected; criteria evaluation receives `facts` as a parameter, exactly as the donor did.
knownDifferences: `ROOT` and `readComputerUseConfig` are not exported: the first existed only to locate `config/app.json`, the second only to read it. Their replacement is the explicit `configBlock` parameter; this is the whole point of the load-purity adaptation.

A caller that relied on the donor silently reading `config/app.json` must now pass that block as the second argument of `resolveComputerUseOptions` or the third of `createContract`. With no block, resolution is identical to the donor running against a missing or damaged config file.

`target.cjs` is only partially carried, as a seam inside `action.mjs` (`normalizeTarget`, `describeTarget` and their private helpers). `resolveTarget`, `revalidate`, the geometric/semantic/accessibility/window matching and the revalidation thresholds stay in the `target-guard` module; `TARGET_MOVEMENT` is present here only because the donor vocabulary file defines it, and nothing in this module consumes it.

No controllers, drivers, executor, state machine, recovery ladder, evidence log or UI surface is ported: those are other modules of this building or out of the mission's allowed scope. The donor `index.cjs` and `executor.cjs` are deliberately absent.

The donor `constants.cjs` exported its constants as mutable-in-principle objects; the port keeps `Object.freeze` exactly where the donor had it, including the shallow-freeze quirk (the `CU_TRANSITIONS` arrays themselves stay mutable).

Preserved donor defects (each pinned by a test, none repaired): (1) `criteria.cjs` `{ kind, ...input }` lets a caller's raw `kind` overwrite the alias-expanded kind, so `kind: 'file'` survives as `'file'` and evaluates as `unknown`, while `type: 'file'` expands correctly; (2) `target.cjs` `looksLikeSelector` matches any `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*`, so a bare lowercase word such as `'save'` is read as a CSS selector instead of a semantic target; (3) `action.cjs`'s `any` parameter rule falls back to `action.target`, so `DOM_TYPE`/`SELECT`/`FILE_WRITE` validate without their text/value/content parameter whenever a target is present; (4) `action.cjs` `normalizeDestructive(body.destructive || body.safety)` means a falsy `destructive` lets a truthy `safety` block decide the kinds; (5) `contract.cjs` builds plan actions through `normalizeAction(input)` with no options, so `limits.max_retries_per_action` never reaches a step's `retry.maxAttempts`; (6) `contract.cjs` does not normalize a plan envelope's `expected_effect`, it stores the raw value while an action's own `expected_effect` is normalized; (7) `errors.cjs` `redactDetails` reduces any non-plain object (a `Date`, a `Map`) to its enumerable entries, i.e. to `{}`; (8) `constants.cjs` `resolveComputerUseOptions(overrides, null)` throws a raw `TypeError` because `configBlock.workspace` is read unguarded (the donor's own default never produced `null`); (9) `constants.cjs` filters a caller's capability array without de-duplicating (duplicates survive) and returns the frozen `CAPABILITIES` array by identity when the value is not an array; (10) `criteria.cjs` `evaluateCriteria` only normalizes when its input is not an array, so an array of raw criterion objects is evaluated unexpanded (aliases unexpanded, `description` `undefined`); (11) `constants.cjs` `targetMovement.updatePx = null` reads as `0` because `Number(null) === 0` is finite; (12) `criteria.cjs` computes a criterion's `description` *before* it expands `all`/`any`, so an `all`/`any` written with `of` (or with no list at all) crashes with a raw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` instead of reaching the donor's own `needs a non-empty criteria array` error, which is only reachable through an explicit `criteria: []`; (13) `criteria.cjs` `url_matches` / `stdout_matches` / `stderr_matches` with `regex: false` switch from a case-insensitive regular expression to a case-sensitive `String.prototype.includes`, so `'example'` does not match `https://Example.com/x`; (14) `action.cjs` `requiresTarget` returns `true` for every action on its explicit list even when the action carries a raw `point` and no target, and ignores the target list for `MOVE`/`SCROLL`.

VERIFICATION_KINDS (9), VERDICTS (3), SCREENSHOT_LEVELS (0..3), CAPABILITIES (5, order), DESTRUCTIVE_KINDS (8, order), DESTRUCTIVE_MODES (3), SCREENSHOT_RETENTION (5), STEP_RESULTS (5), RUN_STATUS (4)

TARGET_MOVEMENT {stablePx:3, updatePx:10}, TIMING (16 keys, exact ms), STALL {3,2}, RETRY {2,2}, CONTRACT_DEFAULTS (200 steps, 2 retries, 2 stall recoveries, confirm, failure retention, both filesystem escape hatches off) with `allowedCapabilities` identical to CAPABILITIES
resolveComputerUseOptions() resolves the exact donor default object, in donor key order, from an explicit `{}` config block
config block layers limits/timing/safety/vision/workspace/capabilities/autonomy/stall under the caller's overrides; an override always wins
positiveInt keeps only integers > 0 (`'42'` -> 42, `2.5`/`0`/`-1` -> default); timing values are rounded then clamped into 0..300, 0..250, 80..500, 80..1000, 10..1000; target movement is not rounded
an unknown destructive mode falls back to `confirm`; the two filesystem escape hatches are strict `=== true` booleans
CODES holds exactly the donor 49 members in donor order with the donor values, including TRANSPORT_LOST === CONTROLLER_UNAVAILABLE and MODAL_REQUIRES_USER === MODAL_BLOCKING
defaultRetryable is true for exactly the donor 14 code values and false for every other member
ComputerUseError carries name/code/message/details/retryable/controllerId/state, falls back to the code as message, coerces an explicit `retryable`, and redacts details in toJSON
redactDetails matches the donor key pattern (password/passphrase/token/secret/api[-_]?key/credential/authorization/cookie), recurses through objects and arrays, and never inspects values
PARAM_RULES deep-equals the donor per-type requirements (36 types) and EXPECTED_EFFECT_KEYS the donor 24-key expected-effect vocabulary
normalizeAction accepts a type string, an object and the `{action:{...}}` envelope, produces the donor field order, and uppercases `type`

the donor ACTION_INVALID messages and details for: a non-object action, an unsupported/missing type, a missing/empty required parameter, a non-string TYPE text, a non-array HOTKEY keys, a non-string SHELL_EXEC command and an inverted stabilization window
stabilization clamps minimum/maximum into 0..300 and reads `options.settleMinMs` nullish; retry clamps attempts into 0..5 without rounding and backoff into 0..400
expected effects normalize to `{any|all, mode}` with camelCase keys snake-cased, `{}` rejected as signal-less, and an unknown key rejected with the supported list
destructive normalizes true/string/object into `{kinds, explicit}`, defaults an empty kind list to DELETE, and rejects a non-boolean/string/object
describeAction labels the target, redacts sensitive text/value, truncates at 60/80 characters and keeps the donor key order
destructiveKinds derives DELETE/FORMAT/INSTALL/PUBLISH from FILE_DELETE and the donor shell-command patterns, with an explicit destructive block taking precedence

the target ladder TARGET_KINDS (7 rungs, rank order) and normalizeTarget for selector/semantic/accessibility/bbox/point/window/visual/candidate shapes, including `kinds`, `rank` and `primaryKind`, plus every TARGET_INVALID message
CRITERION_KINDS is the donor 22-kind closed list in order; `type` aliases (file/url/dom/text/window/process) expand and the six aliases are the donor's
every criterion description string is the donor string, and all/any report their child count

evaluateCriterion over every kind returns the donor verdict for a fixed injected facts object, and returns `unknown` / `no evidence available` whenever the fact is missing; a throwing fact becomes `unknown` with the donor code
negate flips a known verdict and leaves an unknown verdict unknown; `all` is false on any unsatisfied, unknown on any unknown; `any` is true on any satisfied, unknown on any unknown
no criteria at all yields `{satisfied:true, unknown:false, results:[], skipped:true}`
evaluateCriteria maps results to `{kind, description, verdict, detail}` and treats an unknown criterion as not satisfied
requiresTarget is the donor unconditional list for CLICK/DOUBLE_CLICK/RIGHT_CLICK/DOM_*/ACCESSIBILITY_*/FOCUS/SELECT plus any resolved target, and false for MOVE/SCROLL without one
an all/any criterion written with `of` crashes with a raw TypeError exactly as the donor does, while `criteria: []` reaches the donor's `needs a non-empty criteria array`
`regex: false` matching is the donor's case-sensitive substring test
createContract produces the donor default document field-for-field and key-for-key, trims the goal, and rejects a non-object contract and a missing/blank goal with the donor codes

capabilities dedupe, reject unknown names with the supported list, reject a non-array, and fall back to the effective options; the destructive mode and screenshot retention are closed vocabularies that fail loud
safety defaults (foreground/focus required, no confirm callback), forbidden targets normalized through the target model, allowedCommands null vs forbiddenCommands []
limits clamp (0..5 retries, 0..10 stall recoveries, positive-only timeouts) and fall back to the effective options

plan envelopes normalize id/description/actions/optional/maxAttempts/expectedEffect/when with the donor defaults and `step-N` ids, and an invalid action becomes PLAN_INVALID carrying the donor message `plan step <position> is not a valid action: ...`
hasCapability and assertCapability: the no-contract message, the CAPABILITY_NOT_ALLOWED message and details, and the last-wins details spread
declaredDestructiveKinds filters against the closed donor families; describeContract returns the donor log-safe summary
the resolved config block is an explicit parameter of createContract and resolveComputerUseOptions, and the two-argument donor call shape resolves like the donor's missing-config branch

the donor's shipped `config/app.json` block resolves to values identical to the built-in defaults, so an empty block reproduces the donor's shipped-config resolution exactly (asserted, and confirmed by running the donor's own readComputerUseConfig() against its file)

10 801 randomized differential cases (actions, targets, criteria, plans, contracts, options, retryability, redaction) compared live between the donor modules and this port: zero differences, with the donor's real config block passed as the port's parameter

3 000 randomized target vectors show the seam in `action.mjs` is byte-identical in outcome to the donor `target.cjs` `normalizeTarget`/`describeTarget`, and (checked after the fact) identical to the separately landed `target-guard/target.mjs` for every accepted input, so the unavoidable duplication is behaviorally inert

action schema, per-type parameter rules, expected-effect vocabulary and destructive-kind derivation
success-criteria vocabulary, descriptions, three-valued evaluation and the no-criteria rule
contract goal intake, safety posture, limit clamps, plan envelopes and capability assertion
every donor message string asserted verbatim, with its exact length for the long ones
PORT_ADAPTATION: CommonJS -> ESM, one module per donor file boundary plus an `index.mjs` barrel
the donor's init-time `config/app.json` read becomes an explicit `configBlock` parameter of `resolveComputerUseOptions` and `createContract`; `ROOT` and `readComputerUseConfig` are dropped with it
the two pure target helpers `normalizeTarget`/`describeTarget` are carried inside `action.mjs` because `target.cjs` belongs to the `target-guard` module
DEFERRED: controllers, drivers, executor, state machine, recovery/stall ladder and evidence log
channel routing, destructive/focus/modal safety gates and the world state
